backlog.spec: Keep the descriptor-only feature block, the kNN term and the 0.75/0.25 blend structure, but replace the single LightGBM with the simple mean of two LightGBM fits that differ only in capacity: one with num_leaves=8, min_child_samples=15 and n_estimators=700, the other with num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=20 and n_estimators=400, both using the current objective, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed and n_jobs=8. Earlier same-configuration seed bagging did not help because the models were nearly identical; varying tree depth gives genuinely different bias-variance trade-offs, so the average can beat either member. Average the two prediction vectors, then blend that average with the kNN exactly as before. Keep the code to two constructor calls and one mean, with no inner validation.
backlog.title: Average two LightGBMs of different depth on the same descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM in fit_predict with the simple average of two LightGBM models trained on the same RDKit 2D descriptor features with identical hyperparameters (500 trees, lr 0.03, 15 leaves, subsample 0.8 freq 1, colsample 0.5, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed) but different losses: one with objective='l1' and one with objective='huber' (default alpha). Average their test predictions with equal weight, then keep the existing final blend of 0.75 on that averaged GBM prediction and 0.25 on the Tanimoto kNN. The two losses make different errors on outlier-permeability molecules, so their mean may be more stable than either alone.
backlog.title: Objective-diversity LightGBM average

backlog.spec: Regularize the training targets using Tanimoto neighbors within the training fold. Compute the pairwise Tanimoto similarity matrix of training Morgan bit vectors (the same morgan_bits helper). For each training molecule, take its top 5 most similar other training molecules and set its smoothed target to 0.8 times its own measured value plus 0.2 times the similarity-weighted mean of those neighbors' measured values. Fit the L1 LightGBM and the kNN component on the smoothed targets, while kNN still uses the original labels for its neighbor averages. Blend as before with weights 0.75 and 0.25. This shrinks noisy labels toward the local chemical neighborhood.
backlog.title: Label smoothing by similarity neighborhood

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM as now. Compute its out-of-fold predictions on the training set with 5-fold KFold, using the seed. Then predict the test residuals with a Tanimoto kNN (k=7) fitted to the OOF residuals. Final prediction = lgbm + 0.5*knn_residual_pred. Drop the existing 0.25 kNN blend, or keep it at a smaller weight of 0.1.
backlog.title: Residual kNN correction

backlog.spec: Train 5 L1 LightGBM models, each with a different seed. Set colsample_bytree=0.3 and subsample=0.7 for each, and use all training rows. Average their predictions, then blend 0.75/0.25 with kNN. This differs from the earlier row-subsample bagging because the rows stay full and only the feature randomness changes.
backlog.title: Random-subspace LightGBM bag

backlog.spec: Currently every test molecule receives the same mixture, 0.75 LightGBM + 0.25 kNN. Make the kNN weight depend on how close that molecule actually is to the training set: inside fit_predict compute, for each test molecule, the maximum Tanimoto similarity s to any training molecule using the existing Morgan radius-2 2048-bit bit vectors (reuse morgan_bits and the intersection-over-union matrix already computed in knn_predict, returning it alongside the prediction or recomputing it). Then set a per-molecule weight w = clip(0.45 * s, 0.0, 0.40) and return (1 - w) * lgbm + w * knn. Molecules with a near-duplicate analogue in training lean on the neighbour average, while novel scaffolds fall back almost entirely on the descriptor model, which is the regime the scaffold-split harness emphasizes. Keep the features, the LightGBM hyperparameters and k=7 unchanged; use plain numpy, no extra model.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated blend weight for the kNN term

backlog.spec: Replace the mean of the final blend's tree component with a median-type estimator aligned to MAE. Train an ExtraTreesRegressor with 300 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 3, on the same descriptor and count-Morgan features. At prediction time, get the per-tree predictions with a loop over model.estimators_ and take the median across trees for each test molecule instead of the mean. Use this median as the tree component in place of the LightGBM output. Keep the kNN blend at 0.25. Only the aggregation changes, so the comparison is clean.
backlog.title: Median aggregation over ExtraTrees-style tree outputs

backlog.spec: Switch the existing descriptor-only LightGBM to randomized split selection by passing extra_trees=True (LightGBM's extremely-randomized split threshold mode), keeping the same objective, 500 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, and the unchanged 0.75 LightGBM + 0.25 Tanimoto kNN blend. Randomized thresholds add variance reduction that often helps when many descriptor columns are highly correlated and the training set is small, which is exactly this setting; earlier plain ExtraTrees helped as a family, so the same randomization inside boosting is worth one slot. Because randomized splits learn more slowly, also raise n_estimators to 800 while leaving the learning rate at 0.03. Only the LGBMRegressor keyword arguments change.
backlog.title: LightGBM extra-trees split mode

backlog.spec: The final line of the current script returns 0.75 * lgbm + 0.25 * knn, where knn_predict uses k=7 neighbours with inverse-distance weights on Tanimoto distances over Morgan radius-2 2048-bit fingerprints. Take one small step in both knobs at once: change the blend to 0.80 * lgbm + 0.20 * knn and call knn_predict with k=12. A larger k smooths the neighbour average, which pairs naturally with a smaller blend weight, and prior slots showed that moving the weight up (0.6/0.4 with k=5) hurt, so the untested direction is less kNN with more smoothing. Change only the k default or call argument and the two blend coefficients; leave the fingerprint, the distance metric, the model and the features alone.
backlog.title: kNN blend weight and k micro-sweep: 0.20 weight, k=12

backlog.spec: In the current script the LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors uses learning_rate=0.03 with n_estimators=500. Replace these with learning_rate=0.015 and n_estimators=1200, keeping the objective, num_leaves, subsample, colsample_bytree, min_child_samples, the descriptor-only feature block and the 0.75/0.25 LightGBM/kNN blend exactly as they are. Lower learning rates with proportionally more rounds usually give a smoother, better-averaged fit on small noisy regression targets, and the MAE objective benefits from finer steps. Confirm the job still fits in the 10-minute budget for 15 fits; LightGBM on roughly 210 descriptor columns and 580 rows should remain only a few seconds per fit. No other changes.
backlog.title: Longer, slower boosting: lr 0.015 with 1200 trees

backlog.spec: Keep the current pipeline exactly (L1-objective LightGBM on the RDKit 2D descriptor block, blended 0.75/0.25 with the Tanimoto kNN), and only change the LightGBM hyperparameters to a slightly different capacity point: num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=1200, min_child_samples=20, colsample_bytree=0.6, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1. Everything else, including the kNN and the blend weights, stays untouched. The aim is to test whether the incumbent is sitting on a sub-optimal point of the depth/learning-rate trade-off for 728 molecules; runtime should stay well under a minute per fit.
backlog.title: LightGBM capacity micro-tune

backlog.spec: Add linear_tree=True and linear_lambda=1.0 to the LGBMRegressor, keeping the L1 objective. Use num_leaves=7 and min_child_samples=20 so the leaf linear models stay stable. Keep the descriptor features, and fill NaNs with the median, because linear_tree needs finite values. Keep the kNN blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add domain-prior monotone constraints to the L1 LightGBM. Build the monotone_constraints list over the descriptor columns, which is aligned to the names in Descriptors.descList: set +1 for MolLogP and NumAromaticRings-free lipophilicity terms (MolLogP, MolMR), and -1 for TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, and fr_COO. Use 0 for every other column. Pass the list as monotone_constraints with monotone_constraints_method 'advanced' to LGBMRegressor. Keep the other hyperparameters and the kNN blend unchanged. Caco-2 permeability should fall with polar surface and hydrogen-bond donors, so this constrains the trees toward that prior.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on LightGBM for polarity descriptors

backlog.spec: Several molecules in this dataset are salts or multi-component SMILES (dot-separated), which makes whole-molecule descriptors such as MW, TPSA and logP reflect the counter-ion rather than the permeating species. Add a small standardization helper used by both featurize and the fingerprint path: parse each SMILES, split on fragments with Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True), keep the fragment with the largest heavy-atom count, neutralize trivially chargeable groups only if straightforward (otherwise skip), re-canonicalize with Chem.MolToSmiles and re-parse. Fall back to the original molecule whenever parsing or fragment selection fails so no row is ever dropped. Apply this once at the top of featurize and once inside morgan_bits so the descriptors, the Morgan fingerprints and the kNN all see the cleaned structure. Keep the model, hyperparameters and the 0.75/0.25 blend unchanged, so the slot measures the effect of standardization alone.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment stripping and canonical standardization of SMILES

backlog.spec: Swap the L1 objective of the LightGBM for LightGBM's quantile objective and average three models fit at alpha=0.45, 0.50 and 0.55, all on the same RDKit 2D descriptor features and with the same remaining hyperparameters as now (500 trees, lr 0.03, 15 leaves, subsample 0.8 freq 1, colsample 0.5, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Take the unweighted mean of the three predictions and feed it into the unchanged 0.75/0.25 blend with the Tanimoto kNN. This is a mild smoothing of the median estimate that keeps the MAE-aligned loss but reduces the step-like behaviour of pure L1 boosting on small data.
backlog.title: Averaged quantile-regression LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a third, purely linear component to the ensemble. Build the existing RDKit 2D descriptor matrix, winsorize each column to its training 1st/99th percentiles, standardize with the training mean and standard deviation (guarding zero-variance columns), and fit sklearn RidgeCV over alphas logspace(-1, 3, 13) on the training labels. The final prediction becomes 0.65 * LightGBM + 0.20 * Tanimoto kNN + 0.15 * ridge, with the LightGBM and kNN parts unchanged. A regularized linear model extrapolates smoothly to unseen scaffolds where trees are forced to predict a constant leaf value, so a small linear share may cover the tails that the GBM flattens.
backlog.title: Blend in a ridge regression on robust-scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM half of the model untouched and only strengthen the kNN component: compute the distance-weighted Tanimoto kNN prediction on Morgan radius-2 2048-bit fingerprints at three neighbourhood sizes k=3, k=7 and k=15, and average the three predictions with equal weight to form the kNN term. The final prediction stays 0.75 * LightGBM + 0.25 * (averaged kNN). Averaging over k gives a smoother local estimator: k=3 keeps the sharp nearest-neighbour signal for molecules with a close analogue, while k=15 damps the variance for isolated scaffolds, and the cost is three argsorts on one small distance matrix.
backlog.title: Multi-k Tanimoto kNN average

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the 1st and 99th percentile of each descriptor column on the training features. Clip both train and test features to those bounds before fitting LightGBM. This limits the effect of extreme descriptor outliers such as Ipc and BCUT on the splits. The kNN and the rest stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Quantile-clipped descriptor inputs

backlog.spec: Add a cheap post-hoc calibration. Inside fit_predict, run a seeded 5-fold CV on the training molecules with the current full model (LightGBM + kNN blend) to obtain out-of-fold predictions, fit the single scalar a that minimizes the mean absolute error of mean_y + a * (oof_pred - mean_y) over a small grid a in {0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 1.00, 1.05}, then apply that same shrinkage to the test predictions and finally clip them to the observed [min, max] range of train_y. Keep features, model and blend weights exactly as they are. Scaffold-split predictions on unseen skeletons tend to be over-dispersed, so a slight shrink plus range clipping can take MAE off without touching the model.
backlog.title: Inner-CV shrinkage and range clipping of predictions

backlog.spec: Set extra_trees=True in the LightGBM parameters. Raise n_estimators to 800 to compensate for the weaker trees. Keep the L1 objective, the descriptor features and the 0.75/0.25 kNN blend.
backlog.title: LightGBM extra_trees mode

memo:
Incumbent is slot 17: L1 LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors blended with kNN, mean_adjusted 0.3694 over 2 runs (0.3725/0.3664).

Helped: data/feature changes (descriptors + Morgan counts 0.3781; kNN blend 0.3976) and the switch to L1 LightGBM on descriptors (-0.0086).

Did not help: family swaps (SVR 0.4222, CatBoost 0.4102, RF 0.3953), feature additions (MACCS+atom-pair 0.3836, Crippen/EState 0.3728, EState fingerprint 0.3716, MACCS 0.3703), pruning (0.3797), winsorizing (0.3792), bagging/subsampled LightGBM (0.3709, 0.3764, 0.3923), stronger regularization (0.3761), min-max kNN (0.3793), kernel ridge (0.3740), DART (4.0173). XGBoost runs failed (94.3105).

Small blends (SVR 0.3693, atom-pair 0.3686, Huber 0.3691) are within the noise sd of about 0.0037.

Next: gains are near the noise floor. Try only small LightGBM tweaks (leaves, learning rate) and small kNN weight/k steps. Replicate any candidate before accepting. Avoid more family swaps, feature additions and pruning.
